name: What Changed in the Contract?
description: Compare two versions of a services agreement (1,600 to 2,800 words across both) and list every substantive change by clause number in the new version, with its type and old and new values: a liability cap, fees, notice and payment periods, insurance limits, an auto-renewal clause added, a clause deleted, a "not" inserted or removed, a changed definition and the governing law. The noise must be ignored: a new section that renumbers everything after it, a clause moved word for word, renumbered cross-references, "thirty (30) days" written "30 days", recased headings and American spellings. Listing a non-change costs as much as missing a real one.
hook: Two drafts, fifteen hidden changes and a lot of noise. Would you sign it?
author: Gauntlet Core

cases.prompt:
Our supplier has sent back a revised draft of our services agreement. Before I sign, tell me exactly what they changed.

List every SUBSTANTIVE change between version 1 and version 2 — a change that alters what either party must do, may do, pays or risks. Do NOT list changes that only affect presentation: clause or section renumbering, cross-references renumbered so they still point at the same clause, a clause moved somewhere else with the same words, the same number written differently ("thirty (30) days" / "30 days", "£250,000" / "£250,000.00", "5%" / "5 per cent"), headings, capitals or spelling. Listing a change that is not substantive costs as much as missing one.

For each substantive change give:
- the clause number in VERSION 2 (for a deleted clause, its number in version 1);
- type: one of "amount" (a sum of money), "percent", "days", "months", "years", "hours" (a time period in that unit), "governing_law", "negation" (a "not" added or removed, reversing the clause), "added" (a new clause), "deleted" (a clause removed), "definition" (a change inside a definition in section 1);
- old and new: the old and new values for amount (in pounds), percent, days, months, years and hours (numbers only) and for governing_law (the jurisdiction's name as written); null for negation, added, deleted and definition.
Only list a clause whose own wording changed (or that was added or removed); a clause whose words are unchanged is not listed even if a changed definition affects it.
